{"topic":"app-manual","bytes":1512,"guide":"## WORKFLOWS — start to finish: a script to a finished video, one picture to an ad, the same character in every shot, cheap previews first, letting an AI do it

### Workflow: keep a character or product the same in every shot (Library, @name, identity sheet, voice)

1. Save one clean picture of them to the Library: **More › Save to Library…** on the picture, or **New {Noun}** on a category page. For a character, an **Identity sheet** helps.
2. Write `@name` in every prompt that shows them. Their picture attaches as a numbered reference; See what gets sent shows the words the model receives.
3. For one look across the film, make a Looks item and write `#name` in each prompt.
4. Give a character a voice (their card → **Add voice**). On video models that take one, the voice attaches with the `@name`.
5. Check the reference rail before pressing **Generate**: a tile marked **Not sent** is past the model's limit.

Details: THE LIBRARY; "Prompt box: @ and # mentions, image 1 citations".

Related sections (ask by heading): Library: New dialog Generate form (character sheet, identity prompt, location prompt, style change, source images, Create & Generate) · Library: sheet tools (Identity sheet, Establishing image, turnaround, character sheet, price) · WORKFLOWS — start to finish: a script to a finished video, one picture to an ad, the same character in every shot, cheap previews first, letting an AI do it · Prompt box: pick a model (model picker, search models, families, Face, tools)"}

In Slates, you keep a face consistent by saving the character to the Library and tagging them in each prompt:

1. **Save one clean picture of the character to the Library.** On a picture you like, go to **More › Save to Library…**. You can also start from scratch with **New Character** on the Characters page. A clear, well-lit, front-facing shot works best.
2. **Make an Identity sheet (optional but helpful).** It gives the model more views of the face to work from.
3. **Write `@name` in every prompt the character appears in**, for example: `@Maya walks into the diner`. Their picture is attached to the shot as a numbered reference. To see exactly what the model receives, open **See what gets sent**.
4. **For a consistent overall look** (grade, wardrobe, style), create a **Looks** item and add `#name` to each prompt.
5. **Give them a voice** if you're making video: on the character's card, click **Add voice**. On video models that support voices, the voice is attached automatically whenever you use `@name`.
6. **Check the reference rail before you press Generate.** If a tile says **Not sent**, the model has hit its reference limit and that image won't be used. Remove other references or pick a model that accepts more.

If you tell me which character you're working on, I can point to the controls on your screen or walk you through making their Identity sheet.
